acceptedAnswer.text: It is a free plugin that turns a WordPress site into an online store, with product pages, a cart, checkout, payments and shipping. You own the store and the data, and you choose the hosting and the extensions.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose WooCommerce or Shopify?

acceptedAnswer.text: WooCommerce suits a store that is part of a content-led WordPress site, or one that needs custom logic. Shopify suits a catalogue-led D2C store that wants less upkeep. We give a straight view on the first call. See Shopify development.

mainEntity.name: Can you move our store to WooCommerce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, from another platform or from an older WooCommerce build. We map products, customers and orders first, move them in a test copy, then switch over with redirects so search visibility is protected.

mainEntity.name: Does it work with Indian payments and shipping?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We connect the gateway you choose, such as Razorpay, plus UPI, cards and cash on delivery where it makes sense, and set shipping zones from your courier terms. Tax settings follow your accountant's advice.

mainEntity.name: Who looks after updates and security?

acceptedAnswer.text: A WooCommerce store needs regular updates, backups and monitoring. We set them up at launch, and our website maintenance retainer can run them after.

mainEntity.name: How is this page different from your WordPress page?

acceptedAnswer.text: The WordPress page covers content sites and themes. This page is about the store itself: catalogue, checkout, shipping, tax, orders and the speed of a shop that takes payments.
A scope agreed after a call and written down, so you can see what is included. We do not publish a price list, because the catalogue, integrations and migration drive the work.

hub.sub: A store on WooCommerce is only as good as its catalogue, checkout and upkeep. We build it so shoppers can buy quickly and your team can run it without a developer.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: WooCommerce development is the work of building an online store on WordPress: the catalogue and variations, the cart and checkout, payments, shipping and tax, and the speed and plugin setup behind them. Done well, shoppers buy in a few taps and your team manages orders and stock alone.

answer.chip: A store your team can run

paras: A WooCommerce store is a WordPress site with a shop bolted on, so two things have to work together: the content side and the store side. We plan the catalogue, the checkout, the shipping and tax rules and the plugin list before we write code.

The result is a store that loads quickly on a phone, takes payments the way your buyers prefer, and does not break when an update arrives. For the wider site, theme and editing set-up see WordPress development.

leaks.lede: A store only earns when shoppers can find, choose and pay. Each stage below is where builds go wrong, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Variants and categories added as the range grows.
stages.why: Messy attributes make filters, feeds and stock counts unreliable.
stages.does: We map products, variations and attributes first, so filters and stock work from day one.

stages.breaks: Pages that bury size, price or delivery details.
stages.why: A shopper who cannot choose a size or see delivery leaves.
stages.does: We design product pages with clear variation pickers, photos and delivery information.

stages.breaks: A plugin pile-up that slows the shop.
stages.why: Every plugin adds weight, update work and risk.
stages.does: We keep plugins few, add caching, clean up scripts and test on a phone.

stages.breaks: Long forms, missing payment methods, wrong rates.
stages.why: Every extra field is a reason to leave, and wrong rates eat margin.
stages.does: We set up a short checkout, the payments your buyers use and rates built from your courier terms.

stages.breaks: A shop only the developer can run, with orders you cannot read.
stages.why: If staff cannot manage orders and stock, the shop stalls.
stages.does: We set up tracking, order statuses and stock alerts, train your team and can stay on under maintenance.
